# Registers

*Generated by `scripts/generate/registers.py` from the registers in `requirements/`. Don't edit this file: change the register, then run the script. CI fails if it's out of date.*

Every question, requirement, decision, gap and known limitation, wherever it's kept: each in the register of the source, domain or consumer it's about, tagged with the step of [the process](process.md) it belongs to. The schema is in [`requirements/README.md`](../requirements/README.md). The university, its people and the dates are fictional: the story the films tell, in October 2026.

## Decisions

|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| [DEC-PLN-01](../requirements/exposures/planning/_planning__requirements.yml) | `scope` | consumer `planning` | Scope: the entities Planning's question touches, and no more: learner, credential, award, and credit towards an award. | "Model the university" never ends. A question does. | Noor, data architect, with Planning | 1 Oct 2026 |  |
| [DEC-PRJ-06](../requirements/_project__requirements.yml) | `scope` | project | The conceptual model is written at two levels: a map of the university's domains and key entities (at most 50, modelled or planned, following TCSI), and each core domain and mart's own. Sources, models and exposures each get a top-level folder. | The map shows where each domain sits and what's still to model, without the detail; the detail stays with its owner. What comes in, what's built and who uses it are different things, and each is easy to find on its own. | Noor, data architect | 16 Oct 2026 |  |
| [DEC-STU-01](../requirements/models/student/_student__requirements.yml) | `scope` | domain `student` | A microcredential is a kind of credential, not an entity of its own. So is a badge. | Same identity (the issuer's identifier) and the same lifecycle (issued, maybe revoked). Only the credit points differ. | Mei Tanaka, registrar's office | 2 Oct 2026 |  |
| [DEC-STU-02](../requirements/models/student/_student__requirements.yml) | `scope` | domain `student` | A certificate of attendance isn't a credential. | It says someone was there, not what they can do. | Mei Tanaka, registrar's office | 2 Oct 2026 |  |
| [DEC-STU-05](../requirements/models/student/_student__requirements.yml) | `scope` | domain `student` | Credit counts from the day a result is released or a credential issued, until it's amended or revoked; every change is a new version. | "As at census" needs the credit held on that day, not today. | Mei Tanaka, registrar's office | 8 Oct 2026 |  |
| [DEC-STU-06](../requirements/models/student/_student__requirements.yml) | `scope` | domain `student` | A credential keeps its whole life: issued on a date, revoked on a date, read from every version the source kept. A revoked credential stays, marked revoked. | "As at census" needs what counted then, even if it was revoked since; the wallet shows a revoked credential as revoked, not gone. | Mei Tanaka, registrar's office | 8 Oct 2026 |  |
| [DEC-PRJ-01](../requirements/_project__requirements.yml) | `source_reality` | project | Keys are qualified by where they come from: key sets SIS, LMS and SC. Every hash is kept beside its readable key. | Two systems can use the same-looking key for different people. A hash alone can't be read or checked. | Noor, data architect | 5 Oct 2026 |  |
| [DEC-STU-03](../requirements/models/student/_student__requirements.yml) | `source_reality` | domain `student` | The learner's business key is the student ID, which the registrar's office issues. A learner the student system doesn't know keeps the key of the first system that knew them. | The student system is the system of record for learners. Short-course customers and platform-only learners still need a key. | Mei Tanaka and Noor | 5 Oct 2026 |  |
| [DEC-STU-04](../requirements/models/student/_student__requirements.yml) | `source_reality` | domain `student` | Keys are matched by rules, most trusted first. A person's recorded decision beats every rule, and a decision that two keys are different people stops any rule from matching them. | An email two people share, or a student ID typed wrong, would merge two learners. Some matches only a person can make. | Mei Tanaka, registrar's office | 6 Oct 2026 |  |
| [DEC-PLN-02](../requirements/exposures/planning/_planning__requirements.yml) | `consumer_output` | consumer `planning` | Planning's mart is as it was at census, dated by when things took effect. | Planning compares with the census report. It builds on the same core as the wallet. | Planning, the wallet app team and Noor | 8 Oct 2026 |  |
| [DEC-WAL-01](../requirements/exposures/wallet/_wallet__requirements.yml) | `consumer_output` | consumer `wallet` | The wallet's marts are as they are now. | The wallet shows the learner today. It builds on the same core as Planning. | Planning, the wallet app team and Noor | 8 Oct 2026 |  |
| [DEC-SC-01](../requirements/sources/short_courses/_short_courses__requirements.yml) | `tests` | source `short_courses` | An enrolment with no email - warn when there's any, stop the build when more than five. | One or two walk-ins a term are expected, and the learning team follows them up. More means something broke. | The learning team | 9 Oct 2026 |  |
| [DEC-CRS-01](../requirements/models/course/_course__requirements.yml) | `build` | domain `course` | The award has one source and nothing to resolve, so core_award reads its staging model directly. | An intermediate step is for matching keys, stitching timelines and applying rules; the award needs none of them (docs/conventions.md, Layers). |  |  |  |
| [DEC-PRJ-03](../requirements/_project__requirements.yml) | `build` | project | One group owns staging, intermediate and core while one team builds them; Planning and the wallet each own their marts. Split into projects when teams own their domains. | Groups control who can ref() what within a project. Separate projects add cost that pays off only with separate teams. | Noor, data architect | 12 Oct 2026 |  |
| [DEC-PRJ-05](../requirements/_project__requirements.yml) | `build` | project | The project is organised by domain, following TCSI: student and course in the core, planning and wallet in the marts. Each domain's conceptual model, definitions, column descriptions and physical diagram live in its folder; docs/ keeps the process. | In a large project, each domain owns its meaning and changes it on its own. Definitions kept beside their models are found and reviewed with them. A public reference model gives the domains names others recognise. | Noor, data architect | 15 Oct 2026 |  |
| [DEC-PRJ-08](../requirements/_project__requirements.yml) | `build` | project | DuckDB runs the project here and in CI; Databricks runs it for the university. | Anyone can run it with no account, and the same code runs on the university's platform. |  |  |  |
| [DEC-PRJ-09](../requirements/_project__requirements.yml) | `build` | project | Primary and foreign keys are declared for Databricks and left out on DuckDB. Tests check keys on both. | Databricks records them as information and doesn't enforce them. DuckDB enforces them, and won't rename or drop a table a foreign key points to, which dbt does to rebuild it. |  |  |  |
| [DEC-STU-08](../requirements/models/student/_student__requirements.yml) | `build` | domain `student` | core_credential version 2 is incremental, merged on credential_key, on both engines. | One strategy, merge, that both engines support. |  |  |  |
| [DEC-PRJ-04](../requirements/_project__requirements.yml) | `written_once` | project | Definitions are written once, in the conceptual model, and generated into doc blocks. The physical diagram is generated from the manifest. Descriptions go to Unity Catalog with persist_docs. | Four copies of a definition drift apart. One home, and one direction of sync, keeps them the same. | Jun Park and Noor | 14 Oct 2026 |  |
| [DEC-PRJ-07](../requirements/_project__requirements.yml) | `written_once` | project | A key set is an attribute of the source that issues it, with its keys and their case. Every question, requirement, decision, gap and limitation is an item in a register, in requirements/, in the folder of the source, domain or consumer it's about, tagged with the step of the process it belongs to. | The key set is a fact about a source, so it lives with the source. Registers kept by domain move with the domain when it becomes its own project; one schema lets them be read, checked and indexed together. | Noor, data architect | 17 Oct 2026 |  |
| [DEC-PRJ-02](../requirements/_project__requirements.yml) | `operate_and_evolve` | project | Every core model is versioned, from version 1, and consumers pin the version they read. | A breaking change then arrives as a new version beside the old one, with a deprecation date, not as a surprise. | Noor, data architect | 10 Oct 2026 |  |
| [DEC-STU-07](../requirements/models/student/_student__requirements.yml) | `operate_and_evolve` | domain `student` | core_credential version 2 replaces is_revoked with status (valid, expired or revoked). Version 1 stays until 31 March 2027, built from version 2. | A credential can also expire, and a true/false can't say so. Consumers get time to move; the exposures say who to tell. | Noor and Mei Tanaka | 13 Oct 2026 | Wallet app team |

## Gaps

| ID | Step | Scope | Expectation | Reality | Resolution | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| [GAP-LMS-01](../requirements/sources/learning_platform/_learning_platform__requirements.yml) | `gaps_and_contracts` | source `learning_platform` | A revoked credential is known as revoked. | The learning platform has no revocation flag. It deletes a revoked badge. | **rule in model, fix at source:** A badge that disappears is revoked from the day the platform stopped showing it. A revocation flag and date are requested from the learning team. | agreed |
| [GAP-LMS-02](../requirements/sources/learning_platform/_learning_platform__requirements.yml) | `gaps_and_contracts` | source `learning_platform` | Every learning platform account names its student. | Staff type the student ID in. 4 of 42 current accounts have none (analyses/profiling/profile_null_keys.sql); one holds another student's ID. | **rule in model, fix at source:** Match by email when exactly one student has it; a recorded decision beats the rules. A check of the ID against the student system is requested from the learning team. | agreed |
| [GAP-SC-01](../requirements/sources/short_courses/_short_courses__requirements.yml) | `gaps_and_contracts` | source `short_courses` | An email is written the same way everywhere. | The short-course platform keeps case and spaces as typed: 2 enrolments find no customer as typed, none once trimmed and lower-cased (analyses/profiling/profile_orphans.sql). | **rule in model:** Trim every key and write it in one case before comparing: emails lower case, IDs upper case. The hash upper-cases every key too. | delivered |
| [GAP-SC-02](../requirements/sources/short_courses/_short_courses__requirements.yml) | `gaps_and_contracts` | source `short_courses` | Every short-course enrolment has an email. | Walk-in enrolments can have none. One current enrolment has none, and its certificate can't reach anyone. | **accept:** Warn on any; stop the build above five. | delivered |
| [GAP-SC-03](../requirements/sources/short_courses/_short_courses__requirements.yml) | `gaps_and_contracts` | source `short_courses` | A certificate is a credential. | The short-course platform issues certificates of completion and of attendance in one table. | **rule in model:** Only certificates of completion are credentials. | delivered |
| [GAP-SIS-01](../requirements/sources/student_system/_student_system__requirements.yml) | `gaps_and_contracts` | source `student_system` | One email, one learner. | Two students share a family email, in the student system and on the platform (analyses/profiling/profile_shared_emails.sql). | **rule in model:** An email matches only when exactly one learner has it. The registrar's office decides the rest. | delivered |
| [GAP-SIS-02](../requirements/sources/student_system/_student_system__requirements.yml) | `gaps_and_contracts` | source `student_system` | A change is dated when it happened. | The student system records some changes late: a withdrawal effective on 27 March was recorded on 3 April (analyses/profiling/profile_late_changes.sql). The platforms only say when they recorded a change. | **rule in model, accept:** Use the student system's effective date. Accept that platform dates are the day the platform recorded the change. | delivered |
| [GAP-SIS-03](../requirements/sources/student_system/_student_system__requirements.yml) | `gaps_and_contracts` | source `student_system` | The student system says when an award was conferred. | It has no conferral record. The student's status turns completed. | **rule in model, fix at source:** An award is conferred on the day the first completed version takes effect. A conferral record is requested from the registrar's office. | agreed |
| [GAP-STU-01](../requirements/models/student/_student__requirements.yml) | `gaps_and_contracts` | domain `student` | A status means the same thing everywhere. | Three code sets: ENR, LOA, WD, CMP; active, inactive; 1, 0. | **rule in model:** One canonical set, mapped in seeds/reference/student/status_map.csv, owned by the registrar's office. | delivered |
| [GAP-STU-02](../requirements/models/student/_student__requirements.yml) | `gaps_and_contracts` | domain `student` | A credential can expire. | No source records an expiry. | **accept:** status allows expired; nothing sets it yet. | agreed |

## Known limitations

| ID | Step | Scope | Limitation | What follows |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| [LIM-SC-01](../requirements/sources/short_courses/_short_courses__requirements.yml) | `gaps_and_contracts` | source `short_courses` | An enrolment with no email gives a credential no one holds | It stays out of the core until the learning team adds the email. |
| [LIM-STU-01](../requirements/models/student/_student__requirements.yml) | `gaps_and_contracts` | domain `student` | Revocation dates are the day a source stopped showing a credential as held | A badge: the day the platform stopped showing it. A short-course certificate: the day its enrolment stopped being completed. An award: the day a later record of the same award stopped being completed. It may have been revoked earlier, and a badge deleted for another reason also counts as revoked. |
| [LIM-STU-02](../requirements/models/student/_student__requirements.yml) | `gaps_and_contracts` | domain `student` | A learner the student system doesn't know keeps the key of the first system that recorded them | The learning platform comes first on a tie. The key changes only when they're matched to a student ID, by a rule (a student ID in their platform account, an email only one student has) or by the registrar's office. Their old key stays in int_learner_keys. |
| [LIM-STU-03](../requirements/models/student/_student__requirements.yml) | `gaps_and_contracts` | domain `student` | A learner with two keys in one system gets one value per attribute | Two platform accounts, or two short-course emails - on each date, that system's version recorded last wins. |
| [LIM-STU-04](../requirements/models/student/_student__requirements.yml) | `gaps_and_contracts` | domain `student` | Units count only towards the award they were taken under | Credit moved between awards when a learner changes award is outside this slice. |
| [LIM-PLN-01](../requirements/exposures/planning/_planning__requirements.yml) | `validate` | consumer `planning` | The Planning mart applies identity as it's known today to the census date | The census team matched two learners by hand before publishing on 14 April 2026; the registrar's office recorded the same matches as identity decisions D-001 and D-002 in October. Without those decisions, the mart counts 10 learners, not 12, and the reconciliation fails. |
| [LIM-STU-05](../requirements/models/student/_student__requirements.yml) | `operate_and_evolve` | domain `student` | An incremental run re-merges only what changed | core_credential merges credentials whose source rows were written since the last run, and credentials whose holder was matched to another learner. A change to the model's logic reaches existing rows only with --full-refresh. |
